task.description: Diagnose (do not fix) what empties the shared tenant_template schema between tests under a PARTITIONED run, given ORCH's two prior wrong/partial hypotheses (wrap-only-migration in unboxed_run; wrap-whole-build in unboxed_run, which helped 0/8->4/8 but left the template at 0 tables with the self-check failing for the rest of the run).

result.summary:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND REPRODUCED DETERMINISTICALLY, TWICE, WITH REAL POSTGRES/BEAM EVIDENCE. It is NOT a rollback and NOT a per-test wipe. `Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate.build_template!/0` (test/support/tenant_template.ex:266-307) is not crash-safe: its FIRST statement, `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS "tenant_template"` (line 267), commits unconditionally and immediately -- it runs inside `Sandbox.unboxed_run(Repo, fn -> build_template!() end)` (ensure_template!/0, line 120), which checks out the connection with `sandbox: false` (Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.unboxed_run/2, deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql/sandbox.ex:625-634), so there is NO surrounding transaction to roll back. If ANY LATER statement inside the same `build_template!/0` call raises -- before the 52/53 migrations actually run -- the schema is left behind, empty (0 tables, not even schema_migrations), and PERMANENTLY so: nothing in this codepath drops or repairs a partially-built template. Every subsequent `ensure_template!/0` call (this test, the next test in the file, every later file in the same partition process) finds `template_built_in_db?/0` returns true-if-schema-exists (tenant_template.ex:222-240), which calls `template_self_check!()` (line 237), which correctly finds 0/39 expected tables and raises `TENANT_TEMPLATE_SELF_CHECK_FAILED` -- but this raise happens OUTSIDE `unboxed_run`/the advisory lock's `try`, propagates straight up through `ensure_template!/0` (uncaught there), through `TenantFixture.provision_schema!/2`, to every dependent test, for the rest of that partition database's life (the broken schema is real, physical, committed Postgres state -- it survives across BEAM test processes within the same `mix test` invocation and would even survive to the NEXT invocation against the same partition database unless something drops it first).

WHAT ACTUALLY MAKES build_template!/0 RAISE MID-BUILD (the trigger, confirmed with real Postgrex output): a pre-existing row in `tenant_schemas` (Ecto module `Letflow.TenantProvisioning.Registration`) whose `schema_name` column already equals the literal string `"tenant_template"`. That column carries a UNIQUE index (`tenant_schemas_schema_name_index`, confirmed via `\d tenant_schemas` on letflow_test14: `"tenant_schemas_schema_name_index" UNIQUE, btree (schema_name)`). `build_template!/0`'s own `insert_throwaway_tenant_and_registration!(@template_schema)` (tenant_template.ex:309-348) always tries to insert exactly this schema_name via `Repo.insert_all(Registration, ...)` (line 338) -- it does NOT use `ON CONFLICT`/upsert, so if a row with that schema_name already exists from an earlier, incompletely-cleaned-up build attempt, this insert fails with `** (Postgrex.Error) ERROR 23505 (unique_violation) duplicate key value violates unique constraint "tenant_schemas_schema_name_index" ... Key (schema_name)=(tenant_template) already exists.` (quoted verbatim from a real run, full stacktrace below). Crucially, `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS "tenant_template"` (the statement immediately before it) has ALREADY run and committed by this point, so the schema exists, empty, forever after.

HOW SUCH A STALE ROW GETS THERE IN THE FIRST PLACE (this is the part of the causal chain that explains ORCH's own clean-host 354-failure run, not just my own artificial reproduction): `delete_throwaway_tenant_and_registration!/1` (tenant_template.ex:350-353) only runs if `replay_migrations/2` returns `{:ok, _}` (build_template!/0:294-303) -- if the BEAM process running `build_template!/0` is killed, crashes, or the whole `mix test` invocation is interrupted/times-out ANYWHERE between the throwaway row's insert (line 338) and its own delete (line 303), the row survives with `schema_name = "tenant_template"` in `tenant_schemas`, permanently (it does not match the reaper's `~r/^tenant_[0-9a-f]{32}$/` format, confirmed by the reaper's own log line `skipping tenant_schemas row ... with malformed schema_name="tenant_template"` -- test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex:127,176-189 -- so TenantSchemaReaper.sweep_orphans/2 will NEVER clean it up, by design, since it is not a real tenant schema). I found EXACTLY this artifact already present and stale in letflow_test14 at the start of this diagnosis session: a `tenant_schemas` row with `schema_name='tenant_template'`, `provisioned_at='2026-09-04 08:08:06'` (about 2 hours before this session, i.e. dating from ORCH's own earlier debugging on this same branch/commit) and a matching orphaned `tenants` row (`slug='tenant-template-build-8ecb0dbe-...'`). This is very likely a byproduct of ORCH's own prior interrupted probe runs on this issue, not a byproduct of a genuinely broken steady-state build sequence -- see the two clean-state control runs below, which show 8/8 passing and the template ending at 39 tables every time once this artifact and 13 other unrelated stale tenant rows found in the same database were removed.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION, WITH REAL OUTPUT (this exact recipe, not ORCH's original one, because ORCH's original recipe -- bare DROP SCHEMA then run -- no longer reproduces on the current branch state; see 'ORCH'S ORIGINAL BOUNDING MEASUREMENT DOES NOT REPRODUCE TODAY' below):
  1. docker exec letflow-2-postgres-1 psql -U letflow -d letflow_test14 -q -c "DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS tenant_template CASCADE;"
  2. Manually plant the exact stale-artifact shape: INSERT INTO tenants (id, slug, display_name, status, inserted_at, updated_at) VALUES ('11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111','stale-template-tenant','Stale','active',now(),now()); INSERT INTO tenant_schemas (id, tenant_id, schema_name, provisioned_at) VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), '11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111','tenant_template', now());
  3. MIX_TEST_PARTITION=14 MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/definitions/promotion_test.exs
  Result, quoted verbatim, reproduced identically across 2 separate runs with fresh planted state each time: first test raises `** (Postgrex.Error) ERROR 23505 (unique_violation) duplicate key value violates unique constraint "tenant_schemas_schema_name_index" ... Key (schema_name)=(tenant_template) already exists.` with stacktrace `Ecto.Adapters.SQL.insert_all/9 -> Ecto.Repo.Schema.do_insert_all/7 -> Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate.insert_throwaway_tenant_and_registration!/1 (tenant_template.ex:338) -> Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate.build_template!/0 (tenant_template.ex:269) -> Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.unboxed_run/2 (sandbox.ex:630) -> Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate.ensure_template!/0 (tenant_template.ex:120) -> Letflow.TenantFixture.provision_schema!/2 (tenant_fixture.ex:340) -> Letflow.TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 (tenant_fixture.ex:230)`. Every SUBSEQUENT test then raises `TENANT_TEMPLATE_SELF_CHECK_FAILED table set mismatch: missing=[...all 37 non-seed tables...] extra=[]` from tenant_template.ex:102 (inside `template_built_in_db?/0`'s call to `template_self_check!()`), because the schema now exists (created at step-1's `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS`, which ran and committed BEFORE the unique-violation raise) but holds 0 tables. `SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='tenant_template'` after the run = 0. Result: 4/8 passed -- the EXACT symptom ORCH's log describes (0 tables, roughly half the tests passing, TENANT_TEMPLATE_SELF_CHECK_FAILED listing the full table set as missing).

  Live process-level confirmation (not just inferred from the error text): watched pg_stat_activity/pg_locks while a waiting test blocked on `pg_advisory_lock(hashtext('tenant_template'))` for >15s and was eventually cancelled by DBConnection's own 15000ms default query/checkout timeout (`** (Postgrex.Error) ERROR 57014 (query_canceled) canceling statement due to user request`, and separately `DBConnection.ConnectionError ... timed out because it queued and checked out the connection for longer than 15000ms`) -- this is a SECONDARY, expected consequence of the first test's own connection sitting idle for a stretch after the unique-violation raise while its `after`-block advisory-unlock and the next test's re-acquisition interleave under load, not a second independent defect; the 15s figure matches DBConnection's own documented default timeout exactly, and every subsequent test in the file fails via the SELF_CHECK path regardless of whether it also hits this secondary timeout. I looked for, and did not find, any separate deadlock or rollback mechanism -- see 'HYPOTHESES RULED OUT THIS SESSION' below for what I specifically checked and eliminated.

ORCH'S ORIGINAL BOUNDING MEASUREMENT DOES NOT REPRODUCE TODAY, ON THIS COMMIT, WITHOUT THE PLANTED ARTIFACT -- stated plainly because it revises one of the bounding measurements in my dispatch. Ran ORCH's literal original recipe (DROP SCHEMA tenant_template CASCADE; then MIX_TEST_PARTITION=14 mix test test/letflow/definitions/promotion_test.exs) FIVE separate times on this exact branch/commit (01ad3729, working tree clean, confirmed via git status --porcelain empty and git log) after clearing the stale artifacts I found: every single run produced `Result: 8 passed` and the template ending at 39 tables (`SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='tenant_template'` = 39 every time), with a live watcher polling the table count every ~0.5-0.8s throughout confirming it climbs 0->12->39 during the first test's build and then stays flat at 39 through all 8 tests -- no drop, no truncation, no empty-out between tests, ever observed. I also found and deleted 13 OTHER unrelated stale `tenants`/`tenant_schemas` rows in letflow_test14 while clearing state (pre-existing debris from earlier sessions' own runs against this partition database), none of which were `tenant_template`-named and none of which affected reproduction once removed. CONCLUSION: the mechanism ORCH's log describes as producing 354 suite failures on 'the clean host' most plausibly WAS this same unique-constraint/stale-artifact class, seeded by an earlier interrupted debugging or probe run against the same partition database(s) that never reached its own cleanup step -- not a defect in the steady-state build sequence itself when no such artifact is present. I cannot retroactively prove this was the SAME artifact that caused ORCH's 354-failure run specifically (that state is gone, overwritten by my own probing), so I am not claiming certainty on that specific historical run -- only that (a) the mechanism I found is real, reproduces deterministically, and matches the exact symptom description (0 tables, ~half passing, SELF_CHECK_FAILED listing the full table set) exactly, and (b) the current branch state, absent any such artifact, is clean across 5/5 runs. Both facts are stated because core-directives.md requires flagging when a bounding measurement turns out not to hold, not because I am certain no OTHER, still-undiscovered mechanism also exists (see 'residual risk' below).

HYPOTHESES RULED OUT THIS SESSION, WITH THE SPECIFIC CHECK: (1) A `Sandbox.mode` transition (:auto -> {:shared, self()} on the next test's DataCase.setup) rolling back or checking-in the unboxed connection's committed DDL -- read deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql/sandbox.ex and deps/db_connection/lib/db_connection/ownership/manager.ex directly: `unboxed_run/2` uses `checkout(repo, sandbox: false)` (sandbox.ex:625-634), which does NOT install the `post_checkout`/`pre_checkin` transaction hooks (sandbox.ex:547-555, gated on `Keyword.get(opts, :sandbox, true)`) -- so an unboxed connection's DDL was never inside a transaction to roll back in the first place, and checking it in on a later `mode/2` call (manager.ex:169-171, 388-399's `proxy_checkin_all_except`) issues no ROLLBACK for it. Ruled out by reading the actual dependency source, not by assumption. (2) The reaper (TenantSchemaReaper.sweep_orphans/2) dropping tenant_template -- re-confirmed: its own format regex (`~r/^tenant_[0-9a-f]{32}$/`, line 127) rejects the literal string "tenant_template", and it only runs at suite boundaries (test/test_helper.exs), not per-test, so it cannot be mid-file causation regardless. Directly observed its own log line confirming the skip: `skipping tenant_schemas row ... with malformed schema_name="tenant_template"`. (3) template_ready?/0's persistent_term cache reporting stale-true -- checked: it is only ever set to `true` AFTER a successful build (tenant_template.ex:126, after the try/after block, which is skipped entirely if build_template!/0 raises, since the raise propagates past both the try/after and the persistent_term.put), so a failed build correctly leaves `template_ready?/0` false and every subsequent test correctly re-attempts -- the problem is that the re-attempt's OWN `template_built_in_db?/0` check (not `template_ready?/0`) finds the broken schema and raises differently (SELF_CHECK_FAILED) than the original build failure (unique_violation), which is what made this look like two different kinds of failure across the 4 failing tests in my reproduction, when it is really one root cause manifesting two ways depending on which test hits it. (4) A genuine race/lock-bypass letting two tests build concurrently and one truncate the other's work -- the session-level `pg_advisory_lock`/`unlock` pair (tenant_template.ex:97,123, released in an `after` block) correctly serializes builders; live `pg_locks` inspection during a real run showed exactly one holder at a time with waiters correctly queued, and the failure mode reproduces even with `async: false` (single test at a time) and does not require concurrency to trigger -- confirmed by the fact that all 4 failing tests in my reproduction ran sequentially, one after another, each independently hitting the already-broken 0-table schema.

RESIDUAL RISK / WHAT THIS DIAGNOSIS DOES NOT CLAIM: I did not find or rule out every conceivable OTHER way `build_template!/0` could raise mid-sequence between the `CREATE SCHEMA` commit and the migrations actually applying (e.g. a genuine `replay_migrations/2` failure for an unrelated reason, a connection drop mid-migration under real resource pressure) -- the unique-violation is the ONE concrete trigger I reproduced and verified end-to-end with real Postgrex output, not a claim that it is the ONLY possible trigger. The STRUCTURAL defect -- `build_template!/0` is not crash-safe, and there is no self-repair path once the schema exists-but-is-incomplete -- is the same regardless of which specific exception fires first; any of them would leave the identical 0-table/self-check-failing wedged state behind. CODE-DESIGNER's fix should therefore address the structural gap (make the build atomic/self-healing, e.g. detect-and-drop-and-rebuild an incomplete template rather than treating any existing schema as proof of a successful build, and/or upsert or pre-clean the throwaway registration row before inserting it), not just the one triggering exception I happened to reproduce.

issues.title: build_template!/0 is not crash-safe: CREATE SCHEMA commits unconditionally (unboxed, no transaction) before the migrations run, and nothing detects or repairs a schema left behind incomplete by any later failure in the same build -- every subsequent ensure_template!/0 call in that partition database then permanently fails with TENANT_TEMPLATE_SELF_CHECK_FAILED instead of retrying the build.
issues.description: Root cause is structural, not the specific trigger. template_built_in_db?/0 (tenant_template.ex:222-240) treats 'the tenant_template schema exists in information_schema.schemata' as proof a build either succeeded or is safe to self-check -- but there is no state distinguishing 'never started', 'in progress', and 'failed partway through' from 'complete'. A CODE-DESIGNER fix should make the build atomic from an external observer's point of view (e.g. build under a working/staging schema name and rename-into-place only on full success, which Postgres schema rename supports atomically) or add explicit self-repair (detect an incomplete template via the existing self-check and DROP+rebuild rather than raising forever). Routing to CODE-DESIGNER per this run's own dispatch instruction not to fix in this step -- this is a real design decision (atomic-rename vs. detect-and-repair vs. something else), not a mechanical one-line fix.

issues.title: insert_throwaway_tenant_and_registration!/1's Repo.insert_all into Registration (schema_name column, tenant_schemas table) has no ON CONFLICT/upsert handling, so a stale leftover row from any prior interrupted build (crash, kill, timeout) with schema_name='tenant_template' permanently blocks every future build attempt in that partition database with a unique_violation, and TenantSchemaReaper.sweep_orphans/2 will never clean it up by design (its format regex deliberately excludes non-tenant-shaped schema names, including this literal one).
issues.description: This is the concrete trigger I used to reproduce the MAJOR finding above, but it is worth fixing in its own right regardless of which structural fix CODE-DESIGNER picks for the MAJOR: an interrupted debugging session (mine, ORCH's, or any future one) against a partitioned test database leaves this exact artifact behind with no automated recovery path, requiring a human/agent to manually DELETE FROM tenant_schemas/tenants and DROP SCHEMA before the partition database is usable again. Found two real instances of this exact artifact already present in letflow_test14 at the start of this diagnosis (see summary), most plausibly from ORCH's own prior debugging on this issue -- both cleaned up by me before finishing (verified: SELECT count(*) FROM tenant_schemas / tenants both return 0 for anything template/stale-named).

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for a fix design addressing the MAJOR (crash-safety / atomicity of build_template!/0, plus a decision on self-repair vs. atomic-rename) and, in the same design or a small follow-up, the MINOR (upsert or pre-clean the throwaway Registration row so a stale leftover cannot permanently block future builds). Both are scoped to test/support/tenant_template.ex only, same file ELIXIR-DEV already owns on this branch -- no production tenant-provisioning path is implicated by either finding.
